annotation.kind: source selection, Model 1.5 execution interface, Theorem 4.4 event certificate, and equation (4.20) aggregation

assumptions: The Householder QR run has positive column dimension n and m >= n, and its computed output RHat is upper trapezoidal.
The scalar computation obeys Model 1.5: equation (1.4), |delta| <= u with 0 <= u < 1, computation-order mean independence, and zero mean under a probability measure.
The local application bound (4.2) holds for every Householder step on an event of probability one, as explicitly assumed in Lemma 4.2 and Theorem 4.4.
The paper constants c5 and c6 are positive natural numbers and lambda > 0.

The input to equation (4.20) is the simultaneous Theorem 4.4 certificate: on one measurable event, the exact orthogonal QR relation and every columnwise bound (4.17) hold, with probability at least p4(lambda,m,n).
Each additive column remainder is an otherwise unscaled O(u^2) function as u tends to zero; no dependence on ||A||, dimensions, or lambda is added beyond what the paper states.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P06 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P06 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p06_t1_householder_qr_frobenius_backward_error {Omega} [MeasurableSpace Omega] {m n : Nat} (A) (model : P06Model15 Omega) (run : P06HouseholderQRRun Omega m n A model) (c5 c6 : Nat) (lambda : Real) ... : exists goodEvent Q DeltaA normwiseRemainder, goodEvent is measurable, normwiseRemainder = O(u^2), the event has probability >= p4 and carries upper-trapezoidal RHat, orthogonal Q, A+DeltaA=Q*RHat, and the Frobenius bound (4.20)
formal_statement.plain_language: On the same event as Theorem 4.4, the computed Householder QR factor has an exact orthogonal backward-error certificate and the Frobenius error bound c6*lambda*sqrt(n)*gammaTilde_m(lambda)*||A||_F plus an unspecified second-order remainder.

informal_proof: Keep the Theorem 4.4 event, Q, DeltaA, RHat, exact factorization, and probability unchanged. Regard the column norms as a finite Euclidean vector. Pointwise (4.17), monotonicity of the Euclidean norm, and its triangle inequality bound this vector by the leading coefficient times the input-column norm vector plus the vector of absolute column remainders. Identify the two column-norm vectors with the Frobenius norms, bound the remainder vector's Euclidean norm by its l1 norm, and choose sum_j |remainder_j(u)| as the normwise remainder. A finite sum of O(u^2) functions remains O(u^2).
informal_statement: Equation (4.20), with all inherited Theorem 4.4 Householder-QR, Model 1.5, backward-error, probability, coefficient, dimension, and O(u^2) semantics retained.
